sources.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted book PDF and extracted full text; not an abstract or excerpt.
sources.locator: Chapter 2, §§2.2–2.5, printed pp. 18–42; Chapter 4, §4.2, pp. 71–73; Chapter 5, §5.2, pp. 83–89.
sources.read_locator: Inspected the complete relevant sections: finite entropy and nats/bits (§2.2); finite divergence and entropy bounds (§2.3); conditional entropy, MI, CMI, and chain rules (§2.5); the full finite Fano error-indicator proof (§4.2); and the finite-partition/Radon–Nikodym divergence formula, including the discrete specialization (§5.2).
sources.extent: This is one of two independent full-book treatments for the A page. Its stated finite-alphabet scope matches the local pmf formulation. The local carriers supply complete proofs, including zero-support and equality cases, where the source gives only a shorter route.
sources.support: Primary source for finite entropy conventions, finite KL, conditional entropy, MI/CMI, chain identities, Fano, and the finite-to-measurable KL interface.

contents.name: Nats, bits, and zero convention
contents.detail: §2.2, pp. 18–20, explicitly distinguishes natural-log nats from base-2 bits and sets 0 ln 0=0.

contents.name: Finite marginal and conditional pmfs
contents.detail: §§2.2–2.3 use the finite joint pmf, its marginals, and conditional probability ratios; the local lemma proves normalization in full.

contents.name: Finite sum and measurable KL bridge
contents.detail: §2.3 gives the finite divergence convention; §5.2 gives the RN derivative representation and states the discrete pmf specialization. The local proof constructs the finite density directly.

contents.name: Finite log-sum inequality
contents.detail: §2.3, Lemma 2.3.1, gives the finite divergence/Jensen inequality; the local argument extends it to arbitrary nonnegative vectors and records all support and equality cases.

contents.name: Finite conditional entropy
contents.detail: §2.5, pp. 35–36, defines conditional entropy as an average over conditional pmfs.

contents.name: Finite mutual information
contents.detail: §2.5, pp. 36–37, gives the joint-KL and entropy-difference expressions.

contents.name: Finite conditional mutual information
contents.detail: §2.5, pp. 40–41, defines CMI through the conditional-product distribution.

contents.name: Finite KL nonnegativity and equality
contents.detail: §2.3, Theorem 2.3.1, states nonnegativity and equality iff the probability vectors agree.

contents.name: Nats-to-bits conversion
contents.detail: §2.2 sets the two bases; the local theorem proves termwise conversion for every finite information quantity.

contents.name: CMI identity and equality
contents.detail: §2.5, Lemma 2.5.5, gives the conditional chain identity, nonnegativity, and conditional-independence equality case.

contents.name: Entropy and mutual-information chain rules
contents.detail: §2.5, including Corollary 2.5.1, states the finite entropy and information chain rules.

contents.name: Finite Markov data processing
contents.detail: §2.5 derives the finite Markov-chain information inequality from the chain identities and conditional independence.

contents.name: Finite-alphabet Fano inequality
contents.detail: §4.2, Lemma 4.2.1, gives the full error-indicator proof and the same-alphabet m−1 bound.

contents.name: Fano with erasure/out-of-alphabet estimates
contents.detail: §4.2 supplies the error-indicator method; the local proof separately handles arbitrary finite estimate values and uses m choices on the error event.

contents.name: Binary entropy and extremizers
contents.detail: §§2.2–2.3 give finite entropy conventions and the uniform-distribution maximum; the local verification proves the unique maximizer from KL equality to the uniform binary law and checks endpoints.

contents.name: Directional and infinite KL example
contents.detail: §2.3 states the directional divergence and absolute-continuity support convention; the local example computes both orders explicitly.

contents.name: Independent and deterministic information
contents.detail: §2.5 gives MI as joint KL and as an entropy reduction; the local proof computes independence and deterministic fibers directly.

sources.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete Cambridge University Press author-prepublication book PDF, dated August 2024; not an abstract or excerpt.
sources.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, printed pp. 9–13; Chapter 2, §§2.1 and 2.5, pp. 21–22 and 31–35; Chapter 3, §§3.1–3.6, pp. 41–58.
sources.read_locator: Inspected the complete relevant sections: finite entropy and conditional entropy with chain-rule proof (§1.1); discrete KL support, RN definition, divergence chain rule, and data processing (§§2.1, 2.5); MI and CMI definitions, conditional-independence equality, chain rule, DPI, and the complete randomized-estimator Fano statement (§§3.1, 3.4–3.6).
sources.extent: This independent full-book treatment uses base-2 logarithms in the introductory chapter and states the conversion convention. Later chapters formulate general standard-Borel results; only their finite-alphabet special cases are cited here. The local carriers prove the finite statements directly and do not inherit unneeded measure-space hypotheses.
sources.support: Independent treatment for finite entropy, KL, MI/CMI, chain rules, Markov data processing, and randomized-estimator Fano.

contents.name: Nats, bits, and zero convention
contents.detail: §1.1 uses base-2 entropy and the 0 log 0 convention; conversion to nats is the local logarithm identity.

contents.name: Finite marginal and conditional pmfs
contents.detail: §1.1 defines conditional pmfs by joint-to-marginal ratios; the local lemma verifies all normalizations and zero-mass cases.

contents.name: Finite sum and measurable KL bridge
contents.detail: §2.1 gives the discrete support-aware formula and RN definition; the local proof identifies the explicit finite density.

contents.name: Finite log-sum inequality
contents.detail: §§2.1 and 2.5 provide the finite KL support and divergence-processing context; the local proof supplies the complete vector log-sum argument.

contents.name: Finite conditional entropy
contents.detail: §1.1, Definition 1.3, defines conditional entropy as an average over conditional laws.

contents.name: Finite mutual information
contents.detail: §3.1, Definition 3.1, defines I(X;Y)=D(P_XY||P_XP_Y).

contents.name: Finite conditional mutual information
contents.detail: §3.4, Definition 3.6, defines CMI using the conditional product law.

contents.name: Finite KL nonnegativity and equality
contents.detail: §3.1, Theorem 3.2(c), uses KL nonnegativity and equality to characterize independence.

contents.name: Nats-to-bits conversion
contents.detail: §1.1 fixes the base-2 convention; the local result proves the conversion for all finite definitions.

contents.name: CMI identity and equality
contents.detail: §3.4, Theorem 3.7(a), states CMI nonnegativity and its Markov equality case; the finite local proof spells out support and conditional independence.

contents.name: Entropy and mutual-information chain rules
contents.detail: §1.1, Theorem 1.4(e)–(g), proves entropy chain rules; §3.4, Theorem 3.7(b), gives the mutual-information chain identity.

contents.name: Finite Markov data processing
contents.detail: §3.4, Theorem 3.7(c), derives mutual-information DPI and its equality condition from the chain identity.

contents.name: Finite-alphabet Fano inequality
contents.detail: §3.6, Theorem 3.12, explicitly allows randomized estimators through X→Y→Xhat and gives the same-alphabet m−1 bound.

contents.name: Fano with erasure/out-of-alphabet estimates
contents.detail: §3.6 supplies the randomized-estimator Fano route; the local extension proves the m-way error-branch bound without claiming an m−1 term for erasures.

contents.name: Binary entropy and extremizers
contents.detail: §1.1, Example 1.1, gives Bernoulli entropy and its extrema; the local verification rewrites the value as KL from the uniform binary law and handles the endpoints in nats.

contents.name: Directional and infinite KL example
contents.detail: §2.1, equation (2.1), states the discrete support convention; the local counterexample calculates both directions.

contents.name: Independent and deterministic information
contents.detail: §§3.1–3.2 express MI as joint KL and entropy reduction; the local proof computes the finite cases.
